js.2594zrtu294.en: Four coronagraph families as optical trains, each in four planes with a log-intensity profile below. Lyot: an occulting disc blocks the star's image, the light it diffracts lands on the rim of the re-imaged pupil, and a closing Lyot stop removes that rim so the starlight beside the mask falls by a factor of hundreds. Apodised pupil: the pupil's transmission tapers to its edge, the image's rings fade and the core widens. Vortex: a phase ramp that winds twice around the centre throws all of an on-axis star's light outside the pupil, where the stop removes it. Adaptive optics with angular differential imaging: synthetic frames in which speckles stay fixed while the planet turns with the sky; the median of the frames is subtracted, each frame is turned back and the stack reveals the planet.

js.6j56seqj8.en: Four scenes. Transit timing: two planets near a {n0} period ratio tug each other, so the inner planet's transits arrive early and late and an O−C diagram builds up. Secondary eclipse: the planet slips behind its star half an orbit after transit, a much smaller dip, drawn ten times deeper. Phase curve: a tidally locked planet shows more of its hot day side towards occultation, with its peak shifted by winds. Rossiter–McLaughlin: the planet covers the approaching and then the receding half of the rotating star, so the star's measured velocity swings during transit.
